First, to simplify the fraction on the left-hand side, we multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{13\text{i}(2+3\text{i})}{(2-3\text{i})(2+3\text{i})} & =p+\text{i}q \\ \frac{13\text{i}(2+3\text{i})}{(2)^{2}-(3\text{i})^{2}} & =p+\text{i}q \\ \frac{13\text{i}(2+3\text{i})}{13} & =p+\text{i}q \\ \text{i}(2+3\text{i}) & =p+\text{i}q \\ 2\text{i}+3{\text{i}}^{2} & =p+\text{i}q \\ -3+2\text{i} & =p+\text{i}q\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can equate the real parts and the imaginary parts separately.

- Equating the real parts, we get $-3=p.$

- Equating the imaginary parts, we get $2=q.$

Therefore, $p=-3$ and $q=2.$
